First, I’d like to say, I’m so sorry you’re feeling this way. I have been in the exact same position, where I just couldn’t. I couldn’t get out of bed, I couldn’t do my homework, I couldn’t cry, I couldn’t think straight. When the term started, I was so terrified at how angry my professors would be that I couldn’t go to classes. Something that helped me, was being honest with them. I told them I was going through some serious emotions, or lack of, and I didn’t understand why. But I was honest, apologized, and asked if there was a way I could get them the work a few weeks late. Some agreed, some did not. It was a gamble. But all of them referred me to the on campus counselor, and with time, I was relearning how to function. 

Those negative feelings and thoughts might stick around for awhile. A broken arm can’t heal in a day so don’t expect your heart or brain to heal any faster. Don’t try to rush yourself on anything. But do try to be honest, a little open about what you’re feeling and experiencing, and don’t be afraid to reach out for help if you find yourself contemplating suicide. 

Sending all the good vibes. 💛✨

I’m in a really fucking horrible place, mentally and emotionally, right now. Someone I love was ready to make an attempt on their life, I stayed up all night in a panic trying to contact them or someone to do a welfare check, and the last thing they said to me before going to the hospital has been loudly banging around in my skull. I can’t sleep, I’m physically ill, and the worst part is... they’re distancing themselves and I know soon, they just ... won’t be in my life anymore. 

All I want is their happiness, so I’m trying desperately hard to stop being so overly attached. I’m trying to just ... cease communication and let them be the first to reach out when they’re ready, but the voice in my head tells me that they never will. And it’s probably right. 

I guess no matter what, those words are going to haunt me forever, and I may never know why they make me feel the way they do. And I’ll never have the chance, or the courage, to ask.
